title: Genomic DNA Extraction from Mammalian Cells
purpose: To isolate high-molecular-weight genomic DNA from cultured mammalian cells (about 1–5 × 10⁶ cells) suitable for PCR, restriction digestion and Southern blotting.
principle: SDS lysis with EDTA (nuclease inhibition) and proteinase K digestion release DNA [2][3]. Phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol keeps DNA in the upper aqueous phase [1]. Salt-assisted ethanol precipitation, a 70% ethanol wash and redissolving in TE give clean DNA [1][2]. Volumes are a starting point to optimise.

materials.detail: 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 100 mM EDTA, 0.5% SDS [2]
10 mg/mL stock; about 0.5 mg/mL final, added fresh [2]
Cold 1× PBS for washing; optional glycogen carrier (20 µg/µL) [1]

steps.text: Harvest 1–5 × 10⁶ cells, pellet at 300 × g for 5 min, wash once with cold PBS and remove all PBS.
Resuspend the pellet in 0.7 mL lysis buffer by gentle pipetting with a wide-bore tip [2].
Add 35 µL fresh 10 mg/mL proteinase K and mix by gentle inversion [2].
Incubate at 55 °C until the lysate is clear and viscous, on a gently rocking platform if overnight [1][2].
Optional: add RNase A and incubate at 37 °C before extraction [2].
In a fume hood add 0.7 mL phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol. Mix by inversion; do not vortex, to limit shearing [2][3].
Centrifuge at 16,000 × g at room temperature, then move the upper aqueous phase to a new tube with a wide-bore tip, leaving the interphase [1][2].
For cleaner DNA repeat the extraction, then optionally extract with chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1) to remove residual phenol [3].
Add 1/10 volume 3 M sodium acetate pH 6.0, then 1 volume room-temperature 100% ethanol; mix gently. Stringy precipitate may appear [2][3].
Pellet the DNA (30 min at 4 °C, 16,000 × g for small or dilute samples) and remove the supernatant [1][2].
Wash twice with 1 mL 70% ethanol to remove SDS, salt and phenol; spin 2 min each time and remove all liquid [2].
Air-dry the pellet; do not over-dry, which makes DNA hard to dissolve [1].
Dissolve in 50–100 µL TE or nuclease-free water: overnight at room temperature or 5–10 min at 65 °C [1][2].
Measure A260/A280 (target above 1.7–1.8; A260 of 1.0 ≈ 50 µg/mL) and check integrity on a 0.8% agarose gel [2][3].
Store at 4 °C short term or −20 °C long term.

results: Yield of roughly 10–30 µg per 10⁶–5 × 10⁶ cells for fast-dividing lines (typical range; depends on cell type and ploidy).
A260/A280 of 1.7–2.0 and a dominant high-molecular-weight band (>20 kb) with little smear.
Some RNA carries over; it does not block restriction digestion or Southern analysis [2].
controls: Run a gel to confirm DNA integrity
Optional RNase A step if RNA-free DNA is needed
Include a no-cell lysis-buffer blank for the spectrophotometer

troubleshooting.cause: Incomplete lysis, too few cells, lost pellet
troubleshooting.fix: Extend proteinase K; add glycogen; longer 4 °C spin [1]
Re-extract; avoid interphase; wash twice in 70% ethanol [2]
No vortexing; wide-bore tips; keep EDTA [2][3]

safety: Phenol and chloroform are toxic and corrosive: use a fume hood, nitrile or other chemical-resistant gloves, eye protection and a lab coat [1][3].
Dispose of phenol–chloroform waste as hazardous chemical waste; never pour it down the drain.
Treat human-derived cell lines at the biosafety level your institution requires.
